pk.Notes: Rapid oral bioavailability screen: single gavage dose of 300 mg/kg in female BALB/c mice, 4-8 weeks, 15-20 g, two animals per compound, blood from the retro-orbital veins at 20 min, 1, 2 and 4 h, plasma analysed for zinc by ICP-OES and for platinum by ICP-MS. Zinc values are given relative to the control sample because the body carries a baseline zinc level, so they are an increment over background and not a total plasma concentration; the detection limit for zinc was 480 ug/L. Reported series in ug/L: complex 1 2278.50, 3029.50, 1715.50, 935.55; complex 2 727.83, 1023.55, 1191.95, 624.70 at 20 min, 1, 2 and 4 h. Section 2.6 states in one sentence that the 20 min concentration of complex 1 was its Cmax, which contradicts its own series, the abstract and section 2.6 of the next page, all of which give 3029.50 ug/L at 1 h; the value at 1 h is entered and the contradiction kept here. No AUC, clearance, volume of distribution or half-life is reported, and with two animals per group no dispersion is given. For cisplatin only the time of Cmax is stated; the peak of about 52000 ug/L in Fig. 7 is graph-read and is therefore not entered as a reported parameter. logp.method_description: Ultra-pure water and n-octanol were mixed at a 1:1 ratio (v:v) and shaken on a shaker to saturate both phases. A stock solution was prepared by adding the complex (50 μM) to 4 mL of the aqueous phase. Four milliliters of the saturated n-octanol phase was then added to the stock solution. The mixture was further shaken on a shaker for 4 h and centrifuged to separate the two phases. The UV spectra of both the aqueous phase and the saturated n-octanol phase were analyzed using a UV spectrophotometer. LogPo/w was calculated as the logarithm of the concentration ratio of the compound in the saturated n-octanol phase to that in the aqueous phase.

To determine the partition coefficients (P) of2a, 3a or CDDP, the “shake flask” method was used. Octanol-saturated water (OSW) and water-saturated octanol (WSO) were prepared using analytical grade octanol and ultrapure water. The metal complexes were dissolved in WSO and then mixed with OSW in volumetric ratios of 2:1, 1:1 and 1:2. CDDP was dissolved in the OSW containing 200 mM NaCl (to suppress hydrolysis of the chlorido complex) and mixed with WSO in the same manner. Mixing was done by vortexing for 30 min at room temperature to establish the partition equilibrium. To separate the phases, centrifugation was done at 3000 g for 5 min. The aqueous layers were carefully separated from the octanol layer for metal analysis by flameless atomic absorption spectrometry (FAAS). Partition coefficients were calculated using the equation log P = log ([Ir/Pt]WSO/[Ir/Pt]OSW).

Partition coefficients were calculated by the “shake-flask” method (adapted from references [6][8]). Compounds were suspended in H2OmQ saturated octanol. Suspensions were sonicated for 1 h, shaked for 24 h in an orbital-shaker at 120 r.p.m and there were filtered with a 0.2 μm Nalgene syringe filter (Thermo Fisher Scientific). 4 mL aliquots of the filtered solutions were reserved. Aliquots of the filtered solutions (5 mL) were added to equal volume of octanol saturated H2OmQ. The mixtures were shaked for 24 h at 298 K. Then, samples were centrifuged to separate the phases. UV-VIS of the organic phases and the reserved aliquots of the filtered solutions were registered.Cisplatin was suspended in octanol saturated H2OmQ and the suspension was sonicated for 1 h, shaked for 24 h in an orbital-shaker at 120 r.p.m. and filtered with a 0.2 μm Nalgene syringe filter. 4 mL aliquot of the filtered solution was reserved and 5 mL aliquot was added to28equal volume of H2OmQ saturated octanol. The mixture was shaked for 24 h at 298 K and then was centrifuged to separate the phases. UV-Vis spectra of the aqueous phase and the reserved aliquot were registered. Differences in the absorbance at MLCT bands for complexes1-5 (1, 510 nm; 2, 500 nm; 3, 510 nm; 4, 495 nm; 5, 475 nm) and absorption at 270 nm for cisplatin were used to the determination of LogPO/W values.

Partition coefficient of the complexes was measured by the shake-flask method.[4] Briefly,n-octanol saturated water was prepared by mixing an equal volume of octanol and water and shaking on a mechanical shaker for 24 h at room temperature. Solutions of the complexes were prepared in phosphate buffer (PBS, 10 mM, pH 7.4, presaturated with n-octanol, Vwater). About half of the solutions was mixed with a volume of water-saturated octanol (Voctanol) and the mixture was shaken for 24 h at room temperature, followed by centrifugation at 2500 rpm for 1514min to separate different phases. Pt content was quantified in initial and final aqueous phases by ICP-MS. The log PO/W was measured using the following equation log PO/W = log ([C]initial - [C]final)/[C]final.

Partition coefficients were measured by the shake-flask method. Briefly, equal volumes of n-octanol and PBS were mixed, and different concentrations of the compound were added and vigorously shaken for 12 h. Pt content was determined by ICP-MS. The n-octanol–water partition coefficient (LogPo/w) was calculated using the formula LogPo/w = LogCo/Cw, where Co and Cw represent the concentration of the complexes in n-octanol and water, respectively.

The determination of the partition coefficients of target complexes using the classic n-octanol/water shake-flask method can be summarized as follows: First, equal volumes of n-octanol and purified water were mixed and shaken at 37°C for 24 h to allow mutual saturation of the two phases. After standing for 1 h, the phases were separated for later use. The complexes were dissolved in water-saturated n-octanol to prepare solutions at concentrations of 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120 μM. The absorbance of each concentration was measured in triplicate using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer, and the average values were used to construct a standard curve to ensure reliable linearity. Subsequently, n-octanol-saturated aqueous solution was placed in a centrifuge tube, and the target complex was added to prepare a 50 μM test sample. The mixture was shaken at 37°C for 48 h to ensure equilibrium distribution. After standing for 1 h, the phases were completely separated by centrifugation at 2500 rpm for 15 min. The solutions from both phases were sampled using syringes, and their absorbance values were measured in triplicate using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer. The average values were used for subsequent concentration calculations. The lipid phase concentration (Co) was calculated based on the standard curve, and the aqueous phase concentration (Cw) was determined using the principle of mass conservation. The LogPo/w of the complex was calculated using Equation (1): log Po/w = log(Co / Cw)

The shake-flask method was utilized to measure the log Po/w values of the platinum complexes. Octanol and PBS used in this experiment were presaturated by incubation with shaking of the biphasic mixtures at room temperature overnight. 0.3 mL aliquots of PBS solution containing 50 μM Pt(IV) complex (cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin, 1a–d, 2a–d, 2a′–d′, 3a–d, and 3a′–d′) were incubated with the presaturated octanol (0.3 mL) in 2.0 mL tubes. To obtain homogeneous solutions, a 5 min vortex treatment was indispensable. After that, the two-phase mixtures were kept shaking at room temperature for 1 h to establish the partition equilibrium and then separated by centrifugation. After digestion, the platinum content in each phase was determined by ICP-OES. Each sample was tested in triplicate. The log Po/w values were expressed as the average of the results.

logp.method_description: The lipophilicity of investigated dinuclear platinum(II) complexes and cisplatin was determined by measuring of partition coefficient using the “shake-flask” method in two phases system composed of n-octanol and 10 mM pH 7.4 phosphate buffer (containing 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl). The absorbance of platinum(II) complex in the phosphate buffer was measured spectrophotometrically at a wavelength of its absorption maximum. The concentration of platinum complex was calculated from its extinction coefficient at absorption maximum that was previously determined.

The Log Pow determination of platinum(IV) compounds were conducted using the shake flask method. (57) Platinum(IV) compounds were dissolved in 0.9% NaCl w/v ultrapure water (presaturated with n-octanol for 96 h and left to stand overnight). The solutions were sonicated and filtered through Celite to remove undissolved platinum(IV) compounds. The initial concentrations of platinum content were determined by ICP-OES. Subsequently, the platinum(IV) solutions were added an equal volume of n-octanol (presaturated with 0.9% NaCl w/v ultrapure water for 96 h and left to stand overnight). The heterogeneous mixtures were shaken vigorously for 2 h before centrifuging at 4200g for 15 min to achieve phase separation. The final concentration of platinum content in the aqueous phase was determined again by ICP-OES, and the water–octanol partition coefficient was calculated. All experiments were done in triplicates.

Log Po/w values of the platinum compounds were determined using the shake-flask method. (35) The aqueous (0.9% w/v sodium chloride) and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated with each other for 1 week. Drugs were dissolved in the aqueous phase, an equal volume of saturated n-octanol was added, and the solution was mixed vigorously for 30 min (1400 rpm). Thereafter, samples were centrifuged (15 min, 1500 rpm), and the platinum content of the organic and aqueous phases was determined by GF-AAS. The log of the ratio of platinum concentration in the organic and aqueous phases were calculated to determine log Po/w. The results are the mean of three independent experiments. To ensure the accuracy of log Po/w measurements, the platinum amount in the aqueous phase was determined before the beginning of the experiment and compared to the sum of the measured platinum amounts in both solvents at the end of the experiment. The discrepancies ranged from 0.3 to 19.1%.

To determine the partition coefficient (P) the shake flask method was used. Water and n-octanol were pre-saturated with n-octanol and water, respectively. Compounds were first dissolved in water. Three different ratios of octanol/water were used (e.g. 1:1, 1:2 and 2:1). Mixing was done by vortexing for 30 min at room temperature to establish the partition equilibrium. To separate the phases, centrifugation was done at 3000 g for 5 min. The platinum concentrations in both phases were determined by flameless atomic absorption spectroscopy (FAAS) with a UNICAM 989 QZ spectrometer with a GF90 oven and an autosampler. Platinum was measured at 265.9 nm with a lamp current of 80% and 0.2 nm slit opening in ELC graphite cuvettes. As background correction the deuterium lamp compensation was used. The temperature program was divided into 5 steps: 1) 95 °C for 30 s, heating rate 0 °C/min, argon flow 0.1 L/min; 2) 1400 °C for 10 s, heating rate 100 °C/min, argon flow 0.1 L/min; 3) 2500 °C for 3 s, heating rate 100 °C/min, argon flow 0.1 L/min; 4) 2700 °C for 3 s, heating rate 0 °C/min, argon flow 0.2 L/min; and 5) 20 °C for 10 s, heating rate 0 °C/min, argon flow 0.2 L/min

Water or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) was stirred with octanol for 24 h, and then the mixture was centrifuged for 5 min to obtain octanol-saturated water and water-saturated octanol. 1-5 were dissolved in the octanol-saturated water (or PBS for cisplatin) at a typical concentration of 0.05–5 mM, and then they were mixed with water-saturated octanol in volumetric ratios of 1:1, 1:2, and 2:1. All mixtures were prepared in duplicate. The mixtures were vortexed for 0.5 h, and then they were centrifuged for 5 min. The layers were separated carefully using a fine-gauge needle. The Pt content in the layers was analyzed by graphite furnace atomic absorption spectroscopy (GFAAS). The partition coefficient was taken as the ratio of the concentration of Pt in the octanol layer to that in the aqueous layer (P = coct/cwater). The reported error is the standard deviation of six measurements obtained according to this protocol.

Solutions of all platinum complexes were made to approximately 100 μM in 0.15 M potassium chloride solution, which minimized aquation of the complexes. These concentrations were later measured in addition to the samples. Aliquots of the stock solutions (2, 3 and 4 mL) were added to 1-octanol saturated with water (4,3 and 2 mL, respectively) so that the total volume of each mixture was 6 mL. The samples were shaken mechanically for 16 h, after which, all samples were allowed to settle for 48 h. Duplicate aliquots were obtained of the water layer from each experiment, and these aliquots were diluted 1 in 100 in 1% analytical grade hydrochloric acid (Choice Analytical). For the 1-octanol layer, 500 μL aliquots were combined with 500 μL 1% analytical grade hydrochloric acid, and subjected to ultrasonication for 10 min. The samples were centrifuged for 1 min, and 1-octanol removed. The Pt content of the remaining water layer was measured. Pt concentrations were measured with a Varian Zeeman atomic absorption spectrometer (240Z AA) equipped with a GTA 120 graphite tube atomizer and a Pt UltrAA hollow cathode lamp (Agilent Technologies) against a standard Pt solution prepared from a 1000 μg/mL Pt stock in 5% hydrochloric acid (Choice Analytical). The lipophilicity, log(P), was calculated as the logarithm of the partition coefficient between water and 1-octanol: log(P) = log10([Pt]_octanol / [Pt]_water)

The lipophilicity parameter, log Poct, of the eight complexes was determined by measuring in triplicate the partition coefficients of the 1-octanol/water system based on the method reported by Robillard et al. [27]. The solutions were made up to 500 ml (100 μM) in 0.15 M KCl (7.5 × 10-2 mol, 5.59 g) in order to minimise aquation of the complexes. Equal volumes (2 ml) of the aqueous solution and 1-octanol were shaken together mechanically for 24 h. Aliquots were taken from the upper octanol layer and the lower aqueous layer. The water samples were diluted 100-fold with rigorous shaking. Platinum content was determined by graphite furnace atomic absorption spectroscopy (GFAAS). The partition coefficients were expressed as the log10 of the ratio of the platinum concentration in the 1-octanol layer to the platinum concentration in the aqueous layer according to Eq. (1).
The water-octanol partition coefficients of the six toxic complexes and cisplatin were measured using the classical shake-flask method.

The lipophilicity (log P) of the compounds was determined using the shake-flask method [30]. Aqueous (0.9% w/v) sodium chloride and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. Drugs were dissolved at a concentration of 0.30 mg mL- 1 in 2.5 mL of saturated n-octanol, except for cisplatin and carboplatin, which were dissolved in the aqueous phase. An equal volume of immiscible solvent was added, and the solutions were mechanically mixed in plastic tubes for 24 h, followed by centrifugation (6000 rpm, 15 min). After separation, the phases were analyzed using UV–vis spectroscopy to determine the amount of the compound in each phase. The absorption values before and after shaking were compared. The partition coefficient in both phases for each compound was calculated based on the Lambert–Beer Law to determine the log P values. The procedures were repeated five times.

Weighted amounts of compounds were partitioned between equal volumes of water and n-octanol (2 mL) at room temperature using an automatic shaker. Platinum concentrations in the aqueous and organic phase (Caq and Corg, respectively) were measured after appropriate dilution with 2.5% HCl and 1% nitric acid solution in ethanol, respectively. The logarithm of the partition coefficient was calculated as the logarithm of the concentration ratio of the solute distributed in the biphasic system using the following equation: (2) The shake-flask procedure described was preliminary optimized and validated using cisplatin as test compound.

Weighted amounts of the tested platinum complex were suspended by 10 min sonification in 0.9% NaCl water solution, which was previously saturated with n-octanol, and mixed by shaking for 1 h. A simultaneously similar procedure was performed using 5 mL of n-octanol pre-saturated with 0.9% NaCl. Afterward, both suspensions were mixed together, shaken for an additional 1 h, and centrifuged for 5 min. After phase separation and evaporation in vacuo of 1 mL of sample to dryness, the final concentration of Pt was determined by ICP-OES (λ = 265.945 nm) and the partition coefficients were calculated. For the analysis, all samples were dissolved 1:1000 in 2.5% HCl. Each measurement was repeated four times and the final logP was calculated as the arithmetic mean of the four values. Directly after the experiment, all organic and water phases were tested (TLC) for their homogeneity, but no symptoms of decomposition or isomerization of Pt compounds were detected [45,46].

In a n-octanol/water system, the lipophilicity of cisplatin, DN604, C1, and C2 was measured by a shake flask method. An aqueous solution (1.0 mL) of several compounds of equal concentration was mixed with n-octanol, centrifuged at room temperature for 4 h, centrifuged at 2500 rpm, and centrifuged for 15 min to separate the different phases. The solutes in the liquid phase were separated and the platinum content in the initial and final phases was determined by ICP-MS. The log PO/W was calculated using the following equation: log PO/W = log [(Ptinitial - Ptfinal)/ Ptfinal]

The lipid-water partition coefficient was obtained by the standard shake flask method in the 1-octanol/ water system. In brief, the complexes were prepared with 1-octanol to obtain the solution of 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 μM and drawing the standard curve according to the absorbance measured by UV/Vis. Next, the complex solutions (50 μM) prepared with an equal volume of 1-octanol/water saturated system were shaken at room temperature for 48 h. The mixed solutions were centrifuged at 2500 rpm/min for 15 min to separate the two phases. Determination of Cw used the absorbance of the lipid phase and a standard curve. The lipid phase concentration (Cw) could be obtained according to the absorbance of the lipid phase and the standard curve, and the water phase concentration (Co) could be determined by the principle of mass conservation. Obviously, the log P of the complexes was calculated by Equation (1)

The partition coefficients (P) of the investigated platinum complexes were determined by the “shake flask” method. The complexes were dissolved in octanol-saturated water (OSW) containing 200 mm NaCl and mixed with water-saturated octanol (WSO) in volumetric ratios of 2:1, 1:1, and 1:2. Mixing was done by vortexing for 30 min at room temperature to establish the partition equilibrium. To separate the phases, centrifugation was done at 3000 g for 5 min. The layers were separated carefully by using a fine-tip pipette and then analyzed for metal content by flameless atomic absorption spectroscopy (FAAS). The partition coefficients were calculated as the ratio of the concentration of the compound in the octanol layer to that in the aqueous layer, log P=log ([Pt]WSO/[Pt]OSW).

To determine the partition coefficient (P) the shake flask method was used. Octanol-saturated water (OSW) and water-saturated octanol (WSO) were prepared using analytical grade octanol and 0.2 M aqueous NaCl solution (to suppress hydrolysis of the chlorido complexes). Compounds were first dissolved in DMF (compounds cisPt(Ac)(VPA) and cisPt(VPA)2) or water (cisPt(Ac)2 and cisplatin). Mixing was done by vortexing for 30 min at room temperature to establish the partition equilibrium. To separate the phases, centrifugation was done at 3000 × g for 5 min. The aqueous layer was carefully separated from the octanol layer for platinum analysis. Pt was quantified from aliquots taken from the octanol-saturated aqueous samples before and after partition by FAAS. Partition coefficients of Pt complexes were calculated using the equation log P = log ([Pt]WSO/[Pt]OSW).

Lipophilicity was presented as log Po/w values, which were determined by the flask-shaking method. An aliquot of a stock solution of the sample in aqueous NaCl (0.9 % w/v and saturated with octanol) was added to an equal volume of octanol (saturated with 0.9 % NaCl, w/v), and the mixture was shaken overnight at 600 rpm to allow partitioning at 25 °C. After the sample was centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 10 min, the compound content of the organic and aqueous phases was determined by UV absorbance. The lipohydro partition coefficient Po/w (Po/w=Co/Cw=Ao/Aw, A: stands for absorbance) was calculated.

The hydrophobicity (log P) of the series of compounds was determined using a shake-flask method (Albert, 1979). Aqueous (0.9% (w/v) sodium chloride (NaCl) and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. Drugs were dissolved at a final concentration of 300 µM in the aqueous phase. An equal volume of saturated noctanol was added and the solutions mixed for 30 min (45 rpm). Samples were centrifuged (1500 g, 10 min) and the platinum content of the organic and aqueous phases determined by ICP-MS. The log of the ratio of platinum concentrations in the organic and aqueous phases were calculated to determine log P.

To determine the partition coefficients (P) of tested compounds, the “shake flask” method was used. Octanol-saturated water (OSW) and watersaturated octanol (WSO) were prepared using analytical grade octanol and ultrapure water. The platinum complexes and sodium diclofenac were dissolved in the OSW containing NaCl (200 mM) and then mixed with WSO in volumetric ratios of 2:1, 1:1 and 1:2. Mixing was done by vortexing for 30 min at room temperature to establish the partition equilibrium. To separate the phases, centrifugation was done at 3000 g for 5 min. The layers were separated carefully using a fine-tip pipet and then analyzed for Pt content by FAAS. The concentration of diclofenac in individual phases was determined by UV spectrophotometry (λmax = 276 nm). The partition coefficients were calculated as ratio of the concentration of compound in the octanol layer to that in the aqueous layer, log P = log ([Pt]WSO/[Pt]OSW).

The “Shake flask” method was used to determine the partition coefficient of the investigated compounds. Platinum compounds were dissolved in 200 mM NaCl (water solution saturated with octanol) and mixed with octanol (saturated with water) in a 1:1 volumetric ratio. The mixtures were vortexed for 30 min (room temperature) and then the layers were separated by centrifugation (3000g, 5 min). The fractions were analyzed for Pt content by FAAS and log P was calculated as the ratio of compound concentration in the octanol layer versus the aqueous layer [log([Pt]octanol/[Pt]water)].

The log Po/w values of all the carbonate and carboxylate complexes were measured by using a shake-flask method. The presaturated PBS and octanol utilized here were prepared by mixing the two-phase solution and then shaking at room temperature overnight. A portion of 0.5 mL of pre-saturated PBS buffer containing 50 μM Pt(IV) complex was incubated with the pre-saturated octanol (0.5 mL) in a 2 mL tube. The tube containing the two-phase mixtures was shaken at room temperature for 1 h. The two-phase mixtures were isolated by centrifugation and the platinum content in each phase was determined by ICP-OES. The results of log Po/w were expressed as a mean of three independent measurements.

The log P values were obtained by using the shake-flask method and UV–vis spectroscopy. Stock solutions of 1, 2 and NBDHEX were prepared in n-octanol that was pre-saturated with 0.9% NaCl (w/v) solution. Stock solutions of cisplatin were prepared in 0.9% NaCl (w/v) solution that was presaturated with n-octanol. Subsequently, the stock solution was added to an equal volume of n-octanol or 0.9% NaCl (w/v) solution. The heterogeneous mixture was shaken vigorously for 24 h before centrifuging to achieve phase separation. The concentrations of the compounds in the organic and aqueous phases were then determined using UV absorbance spectroscopy. log P was defined as the logarithm of the ratio of the concentrations of the compound in the organic and aqueous phases.

Shake-flask method was used to measure the partition coefficient for CDDP, 1 and 2. Briefly, a mixture of an equal volume of noctanol and phosphate buffer (10 mM, pH 7.4) was shaken on a mechanical shaker at room temperature for 24 h. Saturated solutions of the complexes in phosphate buffer (presaturated with n-octanol) were prepared in an ultrasonic bath followed by a filtration through a 0.2 µm nylon filter. Equal volumes of the solution and n-octanol presaturated with phosphate buffer were mixed and the mixtures were shaken for 24 h at room temperature. Centrifugation was carried out at 2500 rpm for 30 min to separate the two phases. The aqueous layer was carefully separated and the Pt content in initial and final aqueous phases was analyzed by ICP-MS. The log PO/W was measured using the following equation: log PO/W = log [(Ptinitial - Ptfinal)/Ptfinal].

The traditional octanol-water shake-flask method was used to detected the log Po/w values of compounds 1–8. First, n-octanol and PBS were shaken at 37 °C for 48 h to saturate each other, and then separated by separator funnel. Then, the standard curves of concentration-absorbance of compounds in two phases were established by UV spectrophotometer. The complexes 1-8 were dissolved in an equal volume mixture of mutually saturated n-octanol and PBS as described above, respectively, and then stirred in the dark for 24 h at 37 °C. The two phases were separated and determined by UV spectrophotometer, and the concentration in n-octanol (Co) and in PBS (Cw) was obtained ac-cording to the standard curves. The log P were obtained according the formula: log Po/w= log Co/Cw.

The lipophilicity of the drugs was assessed by their octanol/water partition coefficient (Log Po/w). The Log Po/w was determined using the octanol/water shake-flask method. Equal volumes of octanol and pure water were mixed and shaken for 24 h to pre-saturate the solutions. Equal volumes of the pre-treated octanol and water were then mixed, and the target compounds were added until saturation. The mixture was shaken for 48 h and centrifuged at 2500 rpm for 15 min. The Log Po/w values of the synthesized prodrugs were determined by measuring the UV absorbance of the compounds in the octanol and water phases at room temperature using a UV spectrophotometer. The log Pow was calculated using the formula (4-1), where Ao is the UV absorbance of the compound in octanol at a specific wavelength(273 nm), and Aw is the UV absorbance of the compound in the aqueous phase at the same wavelength(273 nm).

Equal volumes of octanol and NaCl-saturated water were stirred at room temperature for 24 hours, and separated to give octanol-saturated water and water-saturated octanol. Five standard concentrations (5, 10, 20, 40 and 60 µM) of the complexes were prepared from the octanol-saturated water. Analysis using UV/vis spectroscopy was used to obtain a calibration curve of absorbance vs. concentration for each complex at its maximum absorbance. Accurate amounts of the complexes were dissolved in the octanol-saturated water (25 mL) to make up a concentration of 50 µM. 3 mL of octanol-saturated water containing the complex was placed in a centrifuge tube and 3 mL of water-saturated octanol was layered on top. Six samples prepared in this manner were shaken for 4 hours using a vibrax machine at 500 g min-1 . The layers were separated and the octanol-saturated water layer was retained for analysis using UV/vis spectroscopy. The average concentration of the six runs was calculated using the calibration graph and maximum absorbance for each complex. Subtraction of the average concentration obtained from the concentration of an unshaken sample in octanol-saturated water gave the final [C]org. The [C]org and [C]aq. were used to determine the partition coefficient log P.

The octanol-water partition coefficients were determined as follows. Water (500 mL, distilled after MilliQ purification) and n-octanol (500 mL) were shaken together for 72 h to allow saturation of both phases (one week for the full separation of the two phases). Approximately 0.5 mg of the complexes were placed into a Falcon tube, and 2 mL of octanol-saturated water and 2 mL of water-saturated octanol were added into the same Falcon of the compound and shacked until the complexes were fully dissolved and divided into the two phases. Biphasic solutions were mixed for ten minutes and then centrifuged for five minutes at 6000 rpm to allow separation. Two aliquots of 500 μL for both phases were placed into metal-free PE tubes and 4 mL of a solution of HNO3Suprapure (dilution 1:1 with MilliQ water) for Ag and Au complexes, or 4 mL of 3HCl : HNO3 (aqua regia) solution Suprapure (dilution 1:1 with MilliQ water) for CDDP, were added to the aliquots to obtain 4 samples for each complex (2 for the water phase and 2 for the octanol phase). The solutions were mineralised at 90 °C overnight and 1.5 mL of MilliQ water were added at the end to have a final volume of 6 mL for each sample. The metal concentration in both phases was determined by ICP-OES.61,62

The water/n-octanol distribution coefficients were determined by the stir-flask method [22], [23]; water-saturated n-octanol and n-octanol-saturated water were prepared by shaking equal volumes of n-octanol and water for one week and allowing the mixture to separate into the respective phases. A UV–visible (UV–vis) calibration curve for each complex in n-octanol-saturated water in the 2–50 μM range was prepared. A mixture of 10 mL n-octanol and 10 mL water (each saturated in the other) was stirred for 1 h at 37 °C, after adding the sample to be analysed. Once equilibrium was reached, the organic and aqueous phases were separated and centrifuged. Finally, the concentration of drug in each phase was measured spectrophotometrically to determine values for Log P = Log [drug in n-octanol]/[drug in water]. Experiments were carried out three times [24].

The UV–Vis absorption spectra of complexes 1 and 2 (30 μM) in the buffer solution (5 mM Tris–HCl/50 mM NaCl, pH = 7.2) were performed with different time interval (0 h, 12 h, 24 h, 48 h). The 1-octanol/water partition constant (logPO/W) of complexes 1 and 2 in the 1-octanol/PBS (phosphate buffered solution) system was evaluated by the shake flask method. Solutions of complexes 1 and 2 (5, 10 and 20 μM) were dissolved in PBS solution that pre-saturated with 1-octanol. An equal volume (2.0 mL) of the solution was mixed with 1-octanol that pre-saturated with PBS and shaken at room temperature for 12 h, and then centrifuged into PBS and octanol phases at 2500 rpm. The log Po/w values were estimated by the shake-flask method33 where a compound is shaken in an n-octanol-water 450 mixture, and after equilibrium, the concentration in one phase is measured. The compounds were dissolved at a concentration of 0.3 mg/mL in 4 mL of n-octanol, except cisplatin was dissolved in the aqueous phase. Instead of water, phosphate buffered saline (PBS) was used to suppress the hydrolysis of the chloride ligands.35 An equal volume of PBS was added to the n-octanol, and the solutions were shaken mechanically for 24 h. After separation, the phases were analyzed by UV-Vis spectroscopy to determine 460 the amount of compound in each phase. The absorption values before and after shaking were compared and based on the Lambert-Beer Law, the concentration ratio in both phases for each compound was calculated to determine the logP values.

The log P values for compounds (L1, 1 and 2) were determined by using the shake-flask method and UU-Vis spectrometer. The 1-octanol used in this experiment was pre-saturated with de-ionized water by overnight incubation with shaking a biphasic mixture of the two at room temperature. A 4 mL solution of the compound (ca. 50 μM) was prepared in pre-saturated octanol and 2 mL was used to record UV-Vis spectrum (250-900nm). The remaining 2 mL solution was incubated with 2 mL water in a 5 mL tube. The tube was covered with aluminium foil and vigorously shaken for 2 h using an automated shaker at 37 °C. The tube was then allowed to stand for 15 min and two layers were separated carefully. The octanol layer was used to record UV-Vis spectrum (250 to 900 nm). The log P values were determined using the following formula: Log P = Log(Absorption at 2 h in octanol / (Absorption at 0 h in octanol - Absorption at 2 h in octanol)). The log P value of cisplatin was measured following a similar procedure except for platinum concentration in aqueous and octanol layer was quantified using ICP-MS. All the experiments were carried out in triplicate.

Equal volumes of 1-octanol and sodium chloride saturated distilled water were stirred for 16 h and separated to give water-saturated octanol and octanol-saturated water. Standard solutions of each complex (5, 10, 20, 40 and 60 µM) were prepared in water-saturated octanol. The calibration curve of absorbance against concentration was determined from the maximum absorbance (λmax) of the standard solutions. Stock solutions of each complex (50 µM) in water-saturated octanol (25 mL) were prepared. Six independent samples were prepared by the addition of the stock solution (3 mL) to a 15 mL Falcon tube followed by layered addition of octanol-saturated water (3 mL). Samples were shaken at 1000 g/min for 2 h using an IKA Vibrax VXC basic shaker. The layers were separated, and the water-saturated octanol layer retained. The concentration of each sample in the watersaturated octanol layer was determined by UV-vis spectroscopy with reference to the individual calibration curves to give an average concentration for shaken samples ([C]final). The concentration of an unshaken sample of stock solution was determined to give [C]initial. The partition coefficient (LogP) was determined with by Eqn1

LogP values of complexes 2-4 were determined from logarithmic ratio of distribution coefficient of complexes in an n-octanol and water biphasic mixture. Stock solutions of 2-4 were made in DMSO with a final concentration of 5mM. 6 µL aliquot from this stock solution was taken and the final volume was made to 500 µL. The octanol-water mixture with a final volume of 500 µL (1:1, v/v) was mixed for 1h at 37 °C using rotor rotating 70 rpm. The aqueous layer was carefully separated from the octanol layer. 75 µL of aqueous layer was digested with 300 µL nitric acid for 3 days at room temperature followed by 4 h at 60°C and the final volume was made to 5 ml using DI water. Similarly, 50 µL of octanol was taken and digested with 300 µL nitric acid for 3 days at room temperature followed by 4 h at 60°C. The final volume of the digested octanol layer was also made to 5 ml using DI water. The metal concentrations in both layers were measured using ICP-MS. The partition coefficients of metal complexes were calculated using the equation LogP = Log ([M] octanol /[M] water).

The "shake-flask" technique was used to evaluate the lipophilicity of complexesRu2L1-Ru2L3 using octanol/water phase partitions. Double distilled water and analytical grade octanol (Sigma Aldrich) were used to produce octanol-saturated water and water-saturated octanol phases. Complexes (1 mg/mL; ethanol/water)have been prepared to 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 μg/mL in water and alternately scaled to 2,4, 6, 8, and 10 μg/mL in octanol, respectively. Equal volumes (50/50) of thecomplexes in the proper concentrations (4 mg/mL) have been shaken for 24 hours atambient conditions. The water and organic fractions have been segregated andcentrifuged when equilibrium was attained. Finally, UV-visible spectroscopy wasused to determine the complex concentration in each phase.13 The concentration of the sample solution was used to calculate the partition coefficients (log P) by adopting the equation,Log P = log [(Ru2L1-Ru2L3) octanol/ (Ru2L1-Ru2L3) water].

After mixing octanol and purified water in a 15-mL centrifuge tube, the mixture was shaken in a constant temperature shaker at 37°C for 24 h to achieve mutual saturation of the two phases, preparing saturated solutions of both phases. After allowing the solution to settle for 1 h, it was separated and kept aside. The complexes were dissolved in water-saturated octanol to obtain solutions of 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120 μM concentrations. UV/Vis absorbance measurements were used to construct a standard curve. Subsequently, using the octanol-saturated solution prepared earlier as the solvent, a 50 μM test sample was prepared. An equal volume of water-saturated solution was added, and the mixture was oscillated at 37°C for 48 h. Afterward, the mixed solution was centrifuged at 2500 rpm for 15 min to separate the two phases. The absorbance of the octanol solution was measured using a UV spectrophotometer, and the drug's concentration in the octanol phase (Co) was calculated using the standard curve. According to the principle of mass conservation, the concentration in the water phase (Cw) was determined, and log Po/w was calculated by Formula (1). Log Po/w = log(Co/Cw)
The lipophilicity of CDDP and Pt6 was measured according to reported mothed 5.

Water or PBS were stirred with octanol for 24 h and then centrifuged for 5 min to obtain octanol-saturated water and water-saturated octanol. The platinum complexes were dissolved in the octanol-saturated water, or PBS for cisplatin, to a typical concentration of 0.03 to 3 mM and then mixed with water-saturated octanol in volumetric ratios of 1:1, 1:2, and 2:1 in duplicate. The mixtures were vortexed for 0.5 h and then centrifuged for 5 min. The layers were separated carefully using a fine-gauge needle and then analyzed for Pt content by GFAAS. The partition coefficient was taken as a ratio of the concentration of platinum in the octanol layer to that in the aqueous layer (P = coct/cwater). The reported error is the standard deviation of the six measurements obtained from this protocol.

The lipophilicity of the [(CH3)2NH2]trans-[RuCl4(HmtpO)2] (1a) and cisplatin was determined using the shake-flask method. Aqueous (0.9% v/v) sodium chloride and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. (1a) and cisplatin were dissolved at a concentration of 0.30 mg/mL in 2.5 mL of saturated aqueous phase. An equal volume of n-octanol was added, and the solutions were mechanically mixed for 30 min, followed by centrifugation. After separation, the phases were analyzed using UV-Vis spectroscopy to determine the amount of the compound in each phase. The partition coefficient (log P) in both phases for each compound was calculated based on the Lambert-Beer Law. The procedures were repeated ten times.
